subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw add a core global agent dry-run mode, and which execution surfaces must be covered before users can trust it as a no-side-effects boundary?
rationale: The missing source surface is clear, but choosing dry-run scope, hook/approval ordering, delegated-client behavior, and unsupported-surface handling is a product and security-boundary decision that automation should not make.

options.title: Define Request-Scoped Contract
options.body: Specify covered execution surfaces, preview/result shape, hook and approval behavior, and unsupported-path errors before implementation; this is the recommended path.

options.title: Fold Into Workflow Modes
options.body: Keep this as a component of the broader Ask/Plan/Modify mode design so one authority model owns preview versus mutation.

options.title: Decline Global Dry-Run
options.body: Keep per-command dry-runs and tool policy hooks as the supported safety mechanisms, then close this direction after maintainer confirmation.

recommendation.title: Define Request-Scoped Contract
recommendation.body: Specify covered execution surfaces, preview/result shape, hook and approval behavior, and unsupported-path errors before implementation; this is the recommended path.
